evidence.note: When XOR-stage reduction and D_OPT sweeps (1,2,3) failed to help or regressed, the agent measured each, recognized the change was worse ('D_OPT=3 worse'), and reverted to the better setting rather than persisting on the falsified idea.

Repeated scheduler-heuristic experiments (critical-path, FIFO, ALAP, engine-prio, tie-break-by-vector) each gave 'same' or worse; agent reverted each and eventually updated its model ('the schedule is essentially deterministic given dependencies'), redirecting away from scheduler tweaks. Some mild circling here.
WAR-removal broke correctness and round-14 broadcast regressed cycles; in each case the agent backed the change out cleanly and returned to the known-good 1783/1753 state.

Genuine cost-model correction on surprises: noted valu went UP yet cycles went DOWN (scheduler packs better), and later that saving 318 valu ops did NOT cut cycles because the region was load-bound — updating the load-vs-valu bottleneck model rather than assuming the prediction held.

The idx_off transform broke correctness multiple times; agent deep-debugged (traced u32 underflow to a missing is_off flag), fixed it, then found it saved valu but not cycles and reverted cleanly to kernel_safe. Preserved hard-won state via kernel_v1/v2/v3/safe backups throughout (steps 84,131,154,171).

Recognized the sub-1500 wall was structural (load floor ~1280) but never actually pivoted the whole gather-based strategy despite repeatedly musing about VLOAD; kept revisiting the same tactic — the main gap versus the level-10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent consistently treats falsified predictions as signals to revise its cost model and reverts cleanly, disciplined by explicit backup copies of known-good states (matching the level-8 anchor: clean reverts, diagnosis of why expectations were wrong, avoiding entrenchment). It repeatedly diagnosed the valu-vs-load bottleneck distinction and corrected its machine model (pause behavior, WAR, scheduler determinism). It falls short of 9-10 because it never pivots the whole gather strategy despite recognizing the structural load floor, shows some flailing across near-identical scheduler heuristics, and re-attempts idx_off after it had already failed once.
